card.name: Election wins in political history
card.fires_on: Words in text about elections and election results, such as 'win', 'a' before 'majority', or 'are' before 're-elected', mostly in Canadian or Indian political history, where a party name would come next.

modes.label: Winning an election
modes.description: The verb or word right after a party or leader, where the text says who won or took office.
modes.example: 1930 - Conservatives, led by R.B. Bennett,<< win>> a majority, defeating the Liberals under Mack

modes.label: Election dates and numbers
modes.description: Digits inside a year or a count in election or voting text.
modes.example: referendum in 1992. The Parti Québécois was re-elected to office in 19<<9>>4, led by Jacques Parizeau

card.writes: It lowers the odds of the word 'party' (and its Chinese and other forms) coming next, and slightly raises words like 'voted'.
card.plain: It fires in election history where a party wins, and it makes the next word less likely to be 'party'.
